questions.prompt: Which of the following farming practices best conserves soil moisture during the dry season?

options.label: A
options.text: Mulching the soil with plant residues
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Mulching covers the soil with dry grass or crop residues, reducing direct evaporation and keeping the soil moist for longer. Burning stubble destroys organic matter and exposes the soil, ploughing along the slope encourages erosion, and removing vegetation leaves the soil bare to the sun.

options.label: B
options.rationale: This option reflects a common misconception; the worked explanation shows why it does not apply here.

options.label: C
options.text: Ploughing the field along the slope
options.rationale: This option reflects a common misconception; the worked explanation shows why it does not apply here.

options.label: D
options.rationale: This option reflects a common misconception; the worked explanation shows why it does not apply here.

questions.workedSolution: Mulching covers the soil with dry grass or crop residues, reducing direct evaporation and keeping the soil moist for longer. Burning stubble destroys organic matter and exposes the soil, ploughing along the slope encourages erosion, and removing vegetation leaves the soil bare to the sun. Therefore the correct answer is A: Mulching the soil with plant residues.

questions.prompt: A maize farmer observes that the older leaves of his plants are turning yellow and growth is stunted. Which soil nutrient is most likely deficient?

questions.prompt: A rectangular maize farm measures 120 m by 80 m. Calculate the area of the farm in hectares. (1 hectare = 10,000 m²)
questions.workedSolution: Area = length × width = 120 m × 80 m = 9,600 m². Converting to hectares: 9,600 ÷ 10,000 = 0.96. Answer: the farm covers 0.96 hectares.

questions.prompt: A water treatment plant adds 0.5 g of chlorine for every 100 litres of water. Calculate the mass of chlorine needed to treat 4,000 litres of water.
questions.workedSolution: Each 100 litres needs 0.5 g, and 4,000 litres contains 4,000 ÷ 100 = 40 units of 100 litres. Mass of chlorine = 40 × 0.5 g = 20 g. Answer: 20 g of chlorine is needed.

questions.prompt: In guinea pigs, black fur (B) is dominant over white fur (b). Two heterozygous guinea pigs (Bb) are crossed. What fraction of the offspring is expected to have white fur?
questions.workedSolution: The cross Bb × Bb gives the genotypes BB, Bb, Bb and bb in equal proportions. Since black is dominant, the BB and Bb offspring are black and only the bb offspring are white — 1 out of 4. Answer: 1/4, or 25%, of the offspring are expected to have white fur.

questions.prompt: A student dissolves 25 g of salt in 100 g of water. Calculate the percentage by mass of salt in the resulting solution.
